Answer: C
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray shows a prominent left superior mediastinal contour (indicated by the arrow) alongside slight left ventricular enlargement, which are classic radiographic signs of a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC). When a PLSVC drains directly into the left atrium (unroofed coronary sinus), it creates a right-to-left shunt that explains the patient's mild hypoxaemia and dyspnoea without pulmonary congestion.
